note: The mini-rubric and the dummy transcripts. FROZEN once written: a transcript edited after a span was verified against it breaks the citation chain, which is the exact failure immutability exists to prevent. Spans are given as quotes, never as offsets, and AAO_Seed resolves them against the composed normalized text, so a fixture and the verifier cannot disagree about bytes.

rubric.proposition: The customer's decision maker has confirmed that budget is secured for this initiative in the current fiscal year.
rubric.guidance: Budget is confirmed when a decision maker states that funds are approved, that they are allocated to this initiative specifically, and that they are available in the current fiscal year.

elements.text: available in the current fiscal year

rubric.why: The guidance text names all three parts, so element resolution is a read rather than an inference and Elements_Basis is Authored. That is the path we want to be the main path.

rubric.proposition: A decision maker for this initiative has been identified on the relationship map.
rubric.guidance: This is satisfied when at least one person on the relationship map carries the buying role of decision maker.

elements.text: at least one mapped decision maker exists

rubric.why: Route P: a predicate over map state, no model. Exercises the route that must never call a charter.

rubric.proposition: The customer has told us who else they are considering and what they value about them.
rubric.guidance: Satisfied when a buyer-side participant names an alternative under consideration and states what that alternative offers them.

elements.text: what the alternative offers them is stated

rubric.why: Route C: a charter reading transcript plus committed state.

rubric.short: Success Criteria Captured Per Decision Maker
rubric.proposition: Each mapped decision maker has stated what success looks like for them personally.
rubric.guidance: For each person on the relationship map carrying the buying role of decision maker, satisfied when that person states a measurable outcome they are accountable for and a timeframe for it.

elements.text: a measurable outcome they are accountable for

rubric.why: Per_Person_Source populated, so the per-person count and the empty-set guard are exercised. Counting people needs a pointer, not a structure.

rubric.proposition: The customer and the seller have agreed an implementation timeline.
rubric.guidance: Satisfied when both sides have agreed when the work would start and when it would be live.
rubric.why: Elements_Basis is deliberately Inferred_Pending: the guidance says 'both sides have agreed when the work would start and when it would be live' without naming its parts as parts, so the decomposition is proposed rather than read. Exercises the ratification path.

rubric.proposition: A relevant reference customer has been discussed with the buying group.
rubric.guidance: Satisfied when a comparable customer is named to a buyer-side participant.

elements.text: it was said to a buyer-side participant

rubric.why: Non-gating, so day-one red is not the only behaviour tested.
